summary: Squaw Butte's lookout dates to 1933 or 1940 depending on the source; the present two-story cab went up in 1981 on BLM land near Emmett, Idaho, and is staffed in fire season.

facts.design: Two-story cab built in 1981 on the south summit (present structure)

access.note: Active staffed lookout on BLM land. A maintained road reaches it, but no source describes visitor entry to the cab.

visit.trail_note: Maintained road to the south end of Peak 5894; 2WD vehicles generally reach the saddle below the lookout.

events.note: Register says a lookout has stood here since 1933; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives an 8x8 cab in 1933
firelookout.com says the first 8x8 cab was developed in 1940; conflicts with 1933
Idaho Fire Lookouts: destroyed by lightning in 1938. The register instead lists a structure replaced in 1938. Conflict noted.
NGS station description dated 1959: corrugated metal building 12 ft square, 24 ft tall. Predates the 1981 cab, so it describes an earlier structure.
Present two-story cab on the south summit
Albert Thompson is the earliest named lookout
Orville and Helen Blessinger, listed for 1962-1983
Doreen Mullins, listed for 2001-2014 by Idaho Fire Lookouts
Climbing guide reports the peak's name was changed from Squaw Butte in 2022. Not checked against a federal name record.

evidence.quote: Squaw Butte - South has hosted a lookout since 1933. Structures were replaced in 1938, 1953 and finally 1981 with the current 2 story building.

corrections.proposed: remove 2.4; no source gives the present cab's height (the 24 ft / 7.3 m figure describes the 1959 structure)
corrections.why: No source gives 2.4 m. The NGS station description quoted on the Idaho Lookouts page gives a corrugated metal building 24 feet tall, about 7.3 m. That description is dated 1959, which predates the 1981 cab, so it does not give the present cab's height. 2.4 looks like a decimal slip; confirm before use.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says a lookout has stood here since 1933. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives an 8x8 cab in 1933. Firelookout.com dates the first 8x8 cab to 1940. All three agree the present cab is 1981. The story presents the disagreement.

The register lists a structure replaced in 1938. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists a 1938 lightning loss. Firelookout.com says lightning destroyed the cab before 1953 without a date. The 1953 replacement is consistent across all three.
A climbing guide says the peak was renamed in 2022. The register (2020) and the lookout pages use Squaw Butte. No federal name record was checked, so the rename is reported only.

notes_for_editor: Early history conflicts across three sources (1933 vs 1940 first cab; 1938 replacement vs 1938 lightning loss). The 1981 present cab, BLM ownership and fire-season staffing agree. The 2.4 m height in the brief has no source; the 24-ft figure comes from a 1959 NGS station description on the Idaho Lookouts page and describes a structure older than the 1981 cab. The 2022 rename is reported only by a climbing guide and should be checked against a federal name record before publishing. Staffing after 2015 is not documented. Visitor access rules were not found.
